fulltext: IT之家 10 月 30 日消息，苹果 HomePod mini 2 智能音箱今日正式发售，提供粉色、绿色、蓝色、白色和午夜色五种外观选项，售价 1,099 元。
HomePod mini 2 搭载 S10 芯片，用户可以仅使用单只扬声器，也可组建立体声组合或配置多房间音频，还可用作 Mac 的默认扬声器。
官方表示，HomePod mini 2 可用于操控联网家居，用户只需下达语音指令，便可进行一系列智能家居操作，包括为家门上锁、在外出时关闭车库、在就寝前拉下百叶窗或关闭灯光。
用户还可以使用家庭 App 自动化操作智能家居配件，并通过创建场景同时控制多个配件。此外，HomePod mini 2 还可用作家居中枢。
苹果 HomePod mini 2 采用全频驱动单元和双无源辐射器，可呈现浑厚低音和清澈高音，支持立体声组合，支持声音识别、温湿度传感，无线连接升级到 Wi-Fi 6E，附带 20W 适配器。

fulltext: The Center Will Not Hold
Industry has drained the state’s water reserves for decades. Data centers are the breaking point.﻿
by Gaby Del Valle

AA hulking gray giant rises from the desert. Inside, engineers create the force behind our phones and computers and appliances, our streaming services and search engines and chatbots and vibe-coded apps and websites. The complex is simultaneously massive and squat, dwarfed by the mountains that surround it, and it is endless. I drive past one building, and then another, and then the ground opens up where construction crews have dug up the earth so a third building can rise. There is a parking lot, and then another, and then another. There is an empty lot on the other side of the street, full of cars and the occasional food truck to feed the thousands of laborers who are busy transforming this expanse of desert into an industrial park. There is dust, so much of it, choking the air.

I stand before the savior of Arizona’s economy. Like all great deities, it demands sacrifice. In the desert, nothing is more precious than water, and water is what must be given — nearly 5 million gallons a day, every day, sourced from Phoenix’s municipal supply. The offering has been well worth it.

All of this is the fruit of the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, the world’s leading producer of microchips. Its Arizona operation is the result of a pre-pandemic gamble Phoenix made to revive its sluggish economy, which never quite rebounded from the Great Recession. Now TSMC’s foundry looms over the city’s outskirts.

TSMC is a success story, one that some local leaders may have hoped to repeat with hyperscale data center developments. The progression may have seemed natural: The Grand Canyon State is not only home to the largest chip factory this side of the Pacific but also 172 data centers, neither of which faced much pushback. But the newer, larger developments being proposed from Phoenix to Tucson demand more of everything — more water, more power, more land — than Arizonans are willing to give. Where TSMC was welcomed with open arms and the first wave of data centers was largely ignored, new developments are facing mass backlash in Arizona, where a grassroots, surprisingly bipartisan coalition of residents has united against data centers.

In reporting this story, I spoke to local activists and economic developers, elected officials and their angry constituents. I sat in on city council meetings where people lined up by the dozens to speak up against data center projects, and in cozy suburban homes where tight-knit groups of former strangers told me about the struggle that brought them together. I pored over maps of Arizona’s dry, cracked landscape with laypeople who, over the past two years, have made themselves experts on zoning and land use and water consumption so they can understand the beast they’re trying to fight. The locals on both sides of this debate claim to want the same thing: a better, more prosperous Arizona. Their visions for achieving it, however, are completely at odds.

In Arizona and elsewhere, data center developers have tried to win over locals by making enticing promises about the jobs, tax revenue, and infrastructure they’ll bring with them. All they ask for in exchange is water — and, they swear, not nearly as much of it as you’d expect. Some hyperscale data centers, like Google’s facility in The Dalles, Oregon, use about 1.5 million gallons a day, about one-third of what TSMC’s Arizona complex consumes in the same timeframe. Those reassurances, however, aren’t enough to assuage Arizonans, who now have to contend with the fact that the state will soon lose access to nearly 30 percent of the water it receives from the Colorado River.

Even now, as people across the country sour on AI and fight against data centers in their communities, TSMC’s Arizona operation hums along without significant opposition. And yet it’s impossible to make sense of why Arizonans are so opposed to new data center development without first understanding why they eagerly welcomed TSMC, even though both industries must contend with the issue that has plagued Arizona since its founding: There isn’t enough water.

For as long as anyone could remember, business in Arizona revolved around the storied “five C’s”: cattle, copper, cotton, citrus, and climate, a catchall for the region’s mild, salubrious winters, which locals say often more than make up for the sweltering summers.
Now the state has a sixth C, Arizona native Christine Mackay tells me. “Chips.”

The TSMC development is, in a sense, Mackay’s doing. As the head of Phoenix’s economic development office, she spearheaded the effort that brought the Taiwanese giant to the Sonoran Desert. In 2020, while the global economy was all but shut down, TSMC made an announcement. The same forces that brought the world to a standstill had created even more demand for TSMC’s products, and in response, TSMC would be opening an advanced semiconductor foundry — a “fab,” in industry jargon — in Phoenix. Initially, TSMC predicted that it would pour $12 billion into Arizona’s economy by 2029. Since then, TSMC’s projected expenditure in the state has ballooned to $265 billion, what the company touts as the largest foreign direct investment in US history.

TSMC just put the finishing touches on its second fab in a formerly desolate swath of north Phoenix, with a third under construction and plans for several more underway. This buildout has been more than a decade in the making. TSMC started shopping around for a US location in 2016. That year, Mackay said, the company put out a request for proposals through a codename. No one won.

“We aren’t a group that takes no for an answer,” Mackay said proudly. Her office asked TSMC executives what they thought Arizona was missing, and then spent the next three years addressing their concerns. In 2019, Phoenix sent a delegation to Taiwan to share a new development plan for a science and technology park, the nucleus of which would be a factory, ideally one of TSMC’s fabs. “They agreed they needed to come back and take another look at Phoenix,” Mackay told me. Her team showed them two locations: Laveen, Arizona, a suburb southwest of Phoenix, and, just north of the city, an undeveloped area roughly the size of Manhattan called Biscuit Flats, so named, Mackay told me, because “it’s as round and flat as a biscuit.”
“That very day,” she recalled, “they said, ‘This could work.’”

What followed was a flurry of development unlike anything the state has ever seen. TSMC has brought more than 3,500 jobs to the state, and an entire economy has sprung up to support the company’s Arizona operation. Much like in Taiwan — where the company accounts for nearly one-tenth of Taiwan’s gross domestic product — TSMC has become, if not the center of the universe, then at least a galaxy unto itself. The company controls an estimated 70 percent of the global chip market, and its contracts with Apple and Nvidia alone make up more than one-third of its annual revenue. (Apple and Nvidia design their own chips, but they don’t produce them. The complex manufacturing process is instead largely outsourced to TSMC.)

TSMC has changed swaths of Phoenix — its landscape, its industries — and it has brought with it jobs and prosperity. Locals fear that the new hyperscale data center developments will do the former but not the latter, consuming resources while contributing little to the community. Mackay, who has worked as an economic developer for over 30 years, didn’t experience significant pushback when she helped court data center developments in the past. “The first 10 data centers I did look like pretty little office buildings,” she said.

The new developments being proposed are neither pretty nor little. Where earlier data centers were inconspicuous, the hyperscale facilities developers want to build in Arizona — often on rural farm or desert land — are both massive and incongruous. Despite the state’s recently acquired reputation for sprawl, there are still plenty of places where, in the quiet desert stillness, you can sometimes hear a pack of coyotes howl in the middle of the night. There are dark-sky corridors and wild animals, ghost towns and saguaro forests. All of this, some locals say, could be sacrificed for the benefit of an industry that also poses an existential threat to humanity. There are ethical questions and environmental ones, debates over zoning and taxes and, most of all, over water. Yet the cities and the outlying suburbs keep growing, spreading in all directions until they’re constrained by geography or bureaucracy or Indigenous sovereignty. And industry, somehow, keeps arriving, thirstier than ever.

Year-round but especially in the summers, Arizonans tailor their routines to the elements. Drivers are careful not to get stuck in dust storms or monsoons. Joggers avoid going out in late mornings and early afternoons, when the heat is at its most intense. And on August 1st, at the peak of monsoon season, the No Desert Data Center Coalition’s protest began in the early evening, when the sun’s punishing rays were starting to give way to a muted desert sunset.

About a dozen people showed up to the rally on the outskirts of Tucson, in front of the 290-acre site where Beale Infrastructure is building a 600-megawatt data center. Every few minutes, Vivek Bharathan, one of the organizers, reminded the protesters to stay hydrated. Children sprayed each other with water guns and dutifully accepted drinks from their parents. Mayra Duron, one of the attendees, brought a cooler of agua de jamaica to share with the group. The magenta beverage, she said, was full of electrolytes. Water — the lack of it, the need for it, the amount required to build a massive data center in the middle of the desert — was top of mind. A hand-painted banner expressed the overarching sentiment: BEALE’S DATA CENTER WILL SUCK US DRY.

“If you feel the heat, please head home,” Bharathan told the small crowd. “It is a hot day, and if they succeed in building a data center here, it’ll be even hotter. We know these things create heat islands that can affect the surrounding area by over 10 degrees Fahrenheit.” Duron, a local macrame artist who incorporates cactus spines into her weaving, said she worried about how rising temperatures would affect the region’s saguaros. “In Phoenix, it’s hyper-industrialized,” she said, “and they’ve seen saguaros die left and right.”

Cars honked in support. Some drivers pumped their fists out their windows as they sped by. Arizonans weren’t riled up about AI in 2019, when the TSMC project was announced, nor did they notice or care much about the previous data centers that were quietly built throughout the state. Things have changed. Tucson, it appears, is united in its opposition to the data center complex dubbed Project Blue. But the buildings are going up anyway.

Information about Project Blue began slowly trickling out in the spring of 2025. First came the name, and some clues: The development, whatever it was, would be on a county-owned plot of land; it would create 3,000 temporary construction jobs and 200 well-paying positions down the road; it would generate $152 million in tax revenue over the next decade; it would be big, and it would be thirsty, and new water lines would be built to keep it satiated. That was all anyone in the know would say, because the county government, which owned the land, signed a nondisclosure agreement with the would-be developer.

The news came out in a mundane, bureaucratic way, as information about prospective land sales in midsize cities often does. In June 2025, Jan Lesher, the Pima County administrator, submitted a 44-page memo to the Board of Supervisors. The words “data center” did not appear until the fourth page. This data center would provide an “unprecedented” $3.6 billion opportunity for Tucson and for the county. There were other details, and there was flattery, and there were promises. Project Blue would use “100% renewable water resources.” Its developer, Beale Infrastructure, would build critical infrastructure at its own expense, including an 18-mile pipe extension and an aquifer recharge facility.

“The boost it could provide to our local economy may well be transformative,” Rex Scott, one of five members of the County Board of Supervisors, said at the time. His colleagues were split. They voted 3-2 to rezone the 290-acre tract, and voted again to sell it to Beale for around $20 million. But it wasn’t a guarantee yet. One of the terms of the deal required Tucson to annex the land and approve the sale, since the city would be on the hook for the land’s water service.

The honeymoon, if there even was one, didn’t last. Just hours after the board’s vote, Tucson Electric Power announced it was looking into a rate hike that would increase customers’ bills by an average of 14 percent. The utility claimed the decision was unrelated to the forthcoming data center. Even still, one of the commissioners who voted to rezone the land and sell it to Beale officially asked to reconsider the rezoning.

Perhaps it was the fact that Tucsonans learned of the data center and the rate hike in such quick succession, coupled with the inescapable news of data centers raising locals’ utility bills, that catalyzed their mass opposition. Maybe it was the Arizona Mirror’s report that Project Blue, combined with another proposed data center, would not only be TEP’s biggest customer but also consume more than four golf courses’ worth of water each year. The fact that Amazon Web Services was reportedly the end client — and that county officials had been discussing the project since 2023, and, according to public records obtained by Arizona Luminaria, signed NDAs prohibiting them from naming the companies involved — certainly didn’t help. Whatever the reason, Beale executives probably weren’t prepared for just how angry the public would be.

Around 200 people showed up to a public information meeting Beale hosted in the auditorium of a local high school in July 2025. Most of them were furious about the data center, or they were worried, or they were scared. Tensions were even higher at the follow-up meeting held at the Tucson Convention Center. Over a thousand people showed up. The boos started before Beale’s representatives got through their introductions, and they continued throughout the night.

Keri Silvyn, one of the attorneys representing Beale, tried to warm up the crowd. “We all have cellphones, we have computers, a number of us have multiple of those in our households,” she said. “Many of the various signs that I’ve seen have QR codes, that if you click on, will take you through a data center in order to get to different sites. The internet is housed in data centers. That’s what they are.” Beale’s team explained that they selected the site because it was far from residential areas, and then they reiterated the now familiar pitch data center developers make to wary communities. Beale said it would pay for a pipeline, and once the pipeline was built the data center would run on reclaimed water. (Until then, however, it would rely on potable water.) The company would pay to clean up contaminated water. It would inject any extra water into local aquifers, eventually making the whole thing “water-positive.” None of this mollified the thousand or so people in the audience, who booed every few minutes.

To no one’s surprise, the opposition mostly came down to water. Locals worried that if the data center came to town, the resource, already so scarce and so precious, would vanish. They cited the fact that Arizona would likely lose more of its Colorado River allotment. They conjured images of even hotter, drier summers.

When it was her turn to speak, Melanie Cooley, an education specialist at the Watershed Management Group, a local habitat restoration nonprofit, conjured up a past familiar to few Tucsonans. “Where we are sitting right now was a forest 125 years ago that adjoined a flowing river that flowed year-round,” she said. “There are people alive today who grew up swimming in the Santa Cruz River.”

Average temperatures in Tucson are now 11 degrees Fahrenheit higher than they were a century ago, Cooley said. About six degrees of that rise can be attributed to global warming. The other five, Cooley explained, are because of changes in the local ecosystem, including the felling of forests and the drying up of rivers like the Santa Cruz. “What we see today when we drive across that river that looks like a big, dry ditch, we take it as normal because it’s been that way for so long. But it isn’t normal. It’s a catastrophe. It’s a catastrophe that was brought on by overpumping of our groundwater and bad development decisions, and Project Blue is another bad development decision.”

Another speaker compared Project Blue to industrial projects of decades past. “This is like déjà vu for me,” he said, listing off economic development projects that were supposed to turn things around for the city: Raytheon; Hughes, the military contractor that preceded it; the Air National Guard. “What did they do? They contaminated our water. To this day, we’re having to deal with that.” Tucsonans had gone to great lengths to conserve their water. “We took our landscaping out, we took our swimming pools out.” He waved over a relative who was holding an infant in a sling. “Can you guarantee us water for future generations?” he asked the Beale representatives. “Can you guarantee water for her generation, my kids’ generation, my grandkids’ generation, and this little baby’s generation?”

Two days after this contentious hearing, a unanimous vote by the Tucson City Council shut down the annexation of the land. At a subsequent meeting, the city adopted new rules for data centers and other large water users. Residents were relieved, but not for long. Three weeks after the city stopped the annexation, effectively killing the development, local reporters confirmed that Beale was moving forward with the data center anyway. County officials and Beale representatives had previously said that the deal was contingent on Tucson’s annexation of the land. Suddenly that was no longer an issue. (Beale declined to comment on why annexation was no longer necessary for the deal.)

Over time, there were other adjustments to the plan: The data center would no longer be water-cooled and would instead rely on closed-loop air cooling. If the shift was intended to win over Beale’s critics, it didn’t work. Members of the No Desert Data Center Coalition claim that air-cooled facilities use more electricity, and, since power plants also use water to cool their systems, air-cooled data centers may actually be more water-intensive, just indirectly, an allegation Beale denies. “The use of air-cooled technology for this project does not increase overall energy use; while the energy allocation is different, the energy use is the same,” Beale spokesperson Tony Burkart, the Beale spokesperson, told The Verge. (Energy generation does require water, though there’s little data on just how much water Arizona’s power plants consume.) The change also cost Beale a tenant: Amazon reportedly pulled out of the project, saying an air-cooled facility wouldn’t meet its needs. Beale declined to disclose whether it has since found a new tenant for Project Blue. “It’s up to our tenants when they choose to announce their investment in a project,” Burkart said.

Still, the project moved forward. The county completed its deal with Beale on Christmas Eve, and Beale promised to bring even more gifts in the form of $15 million in donations, some of which would go toward local STEM and trade school programs. The new year brought more challenges. The state’s attorney general filed an appeal against the Arizona Corporation Commission, the state agency that oversees public utilities, over its approval of a special energy agreement between Beale and TEP. Members of the No Desert Data Center Coalition filed a separate lawsuit alleging that the county’s dealings with Beale violated the state’s open meeting law.

fulltext_cn: 中心将无法保持
几十年来，工业已经耗尽了该州的水资源储备。数据中心是突破口。
作者： Gaby Del Valle

AA巨大的灰色巨人从沙漠中升起。在内部，工程师为我们的手机、电脑和电器、流媒体服务、搜索引擎和聊天机器人以及氛围编码的应用程序和网站创造了力量。这个建筑群既庞大又矮小，与周围的山脉相形见绌，而且是无穷无尽的。我开车经过一栋建筑物，然后是另一栋建筑物，然后地面开辟出来，施工人员挖掘了土壤，因此第三栋建筑物可以升起。有一个停车场，然后是另一个，然后是另一个。街的另一边有一个空地，里面装满了汽车，偶尔还有食品卡车，为成千上万的劳动者提供食物，他们正忙着将这片广阔的沙漠变成一个工业园区。有灰尘，太多了，让空气窒息。
我站在亚利桑那州经济的救世主面前。像所有伟大的神一样，它需要牺牲。在沙漠中，没有什么比水更珍贵，必须提供水—每天近500万加仑，来自凤凰城的市政供应。这个产品非常值得。
所有这些都是全球领先的微芯片生产商台湾半导体制造公司的成果。其亚利桑那州的业务是凤凰城为恢复其低迷的经济而进行的疫情前赌博的结果，该经济从未从大衰退中完全反弹。现在，台积电的铸造厂笼罩在城市的郊区。

台积电是一个成功的故事，一些当地领导人可能希望在超大规模数据中心开发中重复这一故事。这一进展可能看起来很自然：大峡谷州不仅是太平洋沿岸最大的芯片工厂的所在地，而且还有172个数据中心，这两个中心都没有受到太大阻力。但是，从凤凰城到图森的新的、更大的开发项目需要更多的东西--更多的水、更多的电、更多的土地--而不是亚利桑那人愿意给予的。当台积电受到热烈欢迎，第一波数据中心在很大程度上被忽视时，亚利桑那州的新发展面临着大规模的反弹，那里的基层，令人惊讶的两党居民联盟联合起来反对数据中心。

在报道这个故事时，我与当地活动家和经济发展商、民选官员及其愤怒的选民进行了交谈。我参加了市议会会议，数十人排队反对数据中心项目，在舒适的郊区家庭中，曾经的陌生人紧密团结在一起，向我讲述了将他们聚集在一起的斗争。我仔细研究了亚利桑那州干燥、破碎的景观地图，与外行人一起，在过去的两年里，他们已经成为分区、土地使用和水消耗方面的专家，这样他们就可以了解他们试图对抗的野兽。这场辩论中双方的当地人都声称想要同样的东西：一个更好，更繁荣的亚利桑那州。然而，他们对实现这一目标的愿景完全不一致。

在亚利桑那州和其他地方，数据中心开发商试图通过对他们将带来的工作、税收和基础设施做出诱人的承诺来赢得当地人的青睐。他们要求的只是水--而且，他们发誓，几乎没有你想象的那么多。一些超大规模数据中心，如谷歌在俄勒冈州达尔斯的设施，每天使用约150万加仑，约为台积电亚利桑那州综合体在同一时间段消耗的三分之一。然而，这些保证不足以安抚亚利桑那人，他们现在不得不面对这样一个事实，即该州很快将失去从科罗拉多河获得近30 ％的水。
即使是现在，随着全国各地的人们对人工智能感到不满，并与他们社区的数据中心作斗争，台积电在亚利桑那州的业务也在没有明显反对的情况下嗡嗡作响。然而，如果不首先了解为什么亚利桑那州人热烈欢迎台积电，就无法理解为什么亚利桑那州人如此反对新的数据中心开发，尽管两个行业都必须应对自亚利桑那州成立以来一直困扰亚利桑那州的问题：没有足够的水。
只要有人还记得，亚利桑那州的生意就是围绕着传奇的“5C”展开的：牛、铜、棉花、柑橘和气候，这是该地区温和、有益健康的冬季的绝佳选择，当地人说，这些冬季通常可以弥补闷热的夏季。
亚利桑那州本地人克里斯汀·麦凯（ Christine Mackay ）告诉我，现在该州有第六个C。“薯条。”

从某种意义上说，台积电的发展是Mackay在做的。作为凤凰城经济发展办公室的负责人，她带头将这位台湾巨人带到了索诺兰沙漠。2020年，当全球经济几乎关闭时，台积电发布了一份公告。导致世界停滞的同一股力量对台积电的产品产生了更多的需求，作为回应，台积电将在凤凰城开设一家先进的半导体代工厂--用行业术语来说是“晶圆厂”。最初，台积电预测，到2029年，它将向亚利桑那州的经济注入120 $。此后，台积电在该州的预计支出激增至2650亿美元（ $ 2650亿美元） ，该公司称之为美国历史上最大的外国直接投资。
台积电刚刚对其位于北凤凰城一片荒凉地区的第二家工厂进行了最后的装修，第三家工厂正在建设中，并计划再建几家工厂。这个扩建项目已经酝酿了十多年。台积电于2016年开始在美国购物。Mackay说，那一年，该公司通过代号发出了征求建议书。没人赢。

“我们不是一个拒绝的团体，”麦凯自豪地说。她的办公室向台积电高管询问了他们认为亚利桑那州缺少什么，然后在接下来的三年里解决了他们的担忧。2019年，凤凰城派代表团前往台湾，分享科技园区的新发展计划，该园区的核心将是一家工厂，最好是台积电的晶圆厂之一。“他们同意他们需要回来再看看凤凰城，”麦凯告诉我。她的团队向他们展示了两个地点：亚利桑那州拉文（ Laveen ） ，凤凰城西南的一个郊区，以及城市北部的一个名为饼干公寓（ Biscuit Flats ）的未开发区域，这个区域的大小与曼哈顿相当，麦凯告诉我，因为“它像饼干一样圆而平。”
“就在那一天，”她回忆说， “他们说， ‘这可能行得通。’”

随之而来的是一连串的发展，与该州从未见过的情况不同。台积电为该州带来了3500多个就业岗位，整个经济蓬勃发展，以支持该公司在亚利桑那州的运营。就像台湾一样--台积电占台湾国内生产总值的近十分之一--台积电已经成为，如果不是宇宙的中心，那么至少它本身就是一个星系。该公司估计控制着全球芯片市场的70% ，仅与苹果和英伟达的合同就占其年收入的三分之一以上。（苹果和英伟达设计了自己的芯片，但并不生产。复杂的制造过程主要外包给台积电。）
台积电改变了凤凰城的景观和行业，并带来了就业机会和繁荣。当地人担心新的超大规模数据中心开发将起到前者的作用，而不是后者，消耗资源，同时对社区贡献不大。Mackay作为经济开发商工作了30多年，她在过去帮助法院数据中心开发时没有遇到重大阻力。她说： “我做的前10个数据中心看起来像是相当小的办公楼。”

所提出的新发展既不漂亮也不少。在早期数据中心不显眼的地方，开发商希望在亚利桑那州建造的超大规模设施（通常在农村农场或沙漠土地上）既庞大又不协调。尽管该州最近因蔓延而闻名，但在宁静的沙漠中，您仍然可以听到一群土狼在半夜嚎叫。这里有黑暗的天空走廊和野生动物、鬼城和仙人掌森林。一些当地人说，所有这些都可以为一个对人类构成生存威胁的行业的利益而牺牲。有道德问题和环境问题，关于分区和税收的辩论，最重要的是关于水的辩论。然而，城市和偏远的郊区不断发展，向四面八方蔓延，直到它们受到地理、官僚主义或原住民主权的限制。工业，不知何故，不断到来，比以往任何时候都更加口渴。
全年，特别是在夏季，亚利桑那人根据元素调整他们的例行公事。司机要小心，不要被沙尘暴或季风困住。慢跑者避免在炎热的早晨和傍晚外出。8月1日，在季风季节的高峰期，无沙漠数据中心联盟的抗议活动开始于傍晚，当时太阳的惩罚性光线开始让位于柔和的沙漠日落。

大约有十几个人出现在图森郊区的集会上，在290英亩的土地前面，比尔基础设施公司正在那里建造一个600兆瓦的数据中心。每隔几分钟，组织者之一的维韦克·巴拉坦（ Vivek Bharathan ）就提醒抗议者保持水分。孩子们互相喷洒水枪，尽职尽责地接受父母的饮料。其中一位与会者Mayra Duron带来了agua de jamaica的冷却器，与大家分享。她说，洋红饮料中充满了电解质。缺水，缺水的需求，在沙漠中建造大型数据中心所需的数量是首要考虑因素。一幅手绘横幅表达了总体情绪： BEALE的数据中心将把我们吸干。
“如果你感到炎热，请回家，”巴拉坦告诉一小群人。“这是一个炎热的日子，如果他们成功地在这里建立了一个数据中心，它会更热。我们知道这些东西会造成热岛，对周围地区的影响超过10华氏度。Duron是一位将仙人掌刺融入编织的当地宏观艺术家，她说她担心气温上升会如何影响该地区的仙人掌。“在凤凰城，它是超级工业化的，”她说， “他们看到仙人掌左右死去。”
汽车鸣喇叭表示支持。一些司机在飞驰而过时把拳头伸出窗外。2019年，当台积电项目宣布时，亚利桑那州人对人工智能并不感到愤怒，他们也没有注意到或关心之前在整个州悄悄建造的数据中心。事情已经发生了变化。图森似乎团结一致，反对被称为蓝色项目的数据中心综合体。但无论如何，建筑物都在上升。
关于蓝色计划的信息在2025年春天开始慢慢流传。首先是名称和一些线索：开发项目，无论它是什么，都将在县拥有的一块土地上；它将创造3000个临时建筑工作岗位和200个高薪职位；它将在未来十年产生1.52亿美元的税收收入；它将是巨大的，而且会很干渴，并且将建造新的供水管道以保持其饱腹感。所有知情人士都会这么说，因为拥有这片土地的县政府与潜在的开发商签署了保密协议。

这一消息以平凡、官僚的方式传出，而有关中型城市未来土地销售的信息往往如此。2025年6月，皮马县行政长官Jan Lesher向监事会提交了一份44页的备忘录。直到第四页才出现“数据中心”一词。这个数据中心将为图森和该县提供“前所未有”的36亿$机会。还有其他细节，还有奉承，还有承诺。蓝色项目将使用“100%可再生水资源。“其开发商Beale Infrastructure将自费建设关键基础设施，包括18英里长的管道扩建和含水层补给设施。
“它可以为我们当地的经济带来的推动力很可能是变革性的，”县监事会五名成员之一雷克斯·斯科特（ Rex Scott ）当时表示。他的同事们分裂了。他们以3比2的投票结果重新划分了这块290英亩的土地，并再次投票决定以约2000万美元的价格将其出售给Beale。但这还不能保证。其中一项交易条款要求图森吞并土地并批准出售，因为该市将为土地的供水服务承担责任。
蜜月，如果有的话，也没有持续多久。在董事会投票几小时后，图森电力公司宣布正在考虑加息，这将使客户的账单平均增加14%。该公用事业公司声称该决定与即将到来的数据中心无关。即便如此，其中一位投票重新划分土地并将其出售给Beale的委员正式要求重新考虑重新划分。

也许是图森人接连得知数据中心和费率上涨的事实，加上数据中心提高当地公用事业账单的不可避免的消息，催化了他们的大规模反对。也许是《亚利桑那镜报》的报告称，蓝色项目与另一个提议的数据中心相结合，不仅将成为TEP最大的客户，而且每年还将消耗超过四个高尔夫球场的水。据报道，亚马逊网络服务是最终客户，县官员自2023年以来一直在讨论该项目，根据亚利桑那州Luminaria获得的公共记录，他们签署了禁止他们命名相关公司的保密协议，这一事实当然没有帮助。无论出于何种原因， Beale的高管们可能都没有为公众的愤怒做好准备。
2025年7月，约200人参加了Beale在当地一所高中礼堂举行的公共信息会议。他们中的大多数人对数据中心感到愤怒，或者他们担心，或者他们害怕。在图森会议中心举行的后续会议上，紧张局势更加严重。一千多人出现了。嘘声在比尔的代表完成介绍之前就开始了，他们整晚都在继续。

代表比尔的律师之一凯丽·西尔文（ Keri Silvyn ）试图让人群热身。她说： “我们都有手机，我们都有电脑，我们中的许多人在家里都有很多手机。” “我所看到的许多迹象都有二维码，如果你点击，它会带你通过数据中心到达不同的站点。互联网位于数据中心。这就是他们的本质。“Beale的团队解释说，他们选择这个地点是因为它远离住宅区，然后他们重申了现在熟悉的数据中心开发人员对警惕社区的推销。Beale表示，它将支付管道的费用，一旦管道建成，数据中心将使用再生水运行。（然而，在此之前，它将依靠饮用水。）公司将支付清理受污染水的费用。它将向当地含水层注入任何额外的水，最终使整个地下水成为“正水”。“这些都没有安抚观众中的一千多人，他们每隔几分钟就会嘘一声。
出乎意料的是，反对派大都落到了水面上。当地人担心，如果数据中心来到城里，已经如此稀缺和珍贵的资源就会消失。他们引用了这样一个事实，即亚利桑那州可能会失去更多的科罗拉多河配额。他们想象着更炎热、更干燥的夏天。
轮到她发言时，当地栖息地恢复非营利组织流域管理集团的教育专家梅兰妮·库利（ Melanie Cooley ）想起了几个图森人熟悉的过去。她说： “125年前，我们现在坐的地方是一片森林，毗邻一条全年流淌的河流。” “今天有一些活着的人在圣克鲁斯河游泳长大。”

Cooley说，图森的平均气温现在比一个世纪前高出11华氏度。这种上升约6摄氏度可归因于全球变暖。Cooley解释说，其他五个原因是当地生态系统的变化，包括森林的砍伐和圣克鲁斯河等河流的干涸。“今天，当我们开车穿过那条看起来像一条大而干燥的沟渠时，我们看到的是正常的，因为它已经存在了很长时间。但这不正常。这是一场灾难。这是一场灾难，是由于过度抽取地下水和糟糕的开发决策造成的，而蓝色项目是另一个糟糕的开发决策。”

另一位发言者将蓝色项目与过去几十年的工业项目进行了比较。“这对我来说就像似曾相识，”他说，列出了应该为城市扭转局面的经济发展项目：雷神公司;休斯，之前的军事承包商;空军国民警卫队。“他们做了什么？他们污染了我们的水。到目前为止，我们必须处理这个问题。“图森人竭尽全力节约用水。「我们外出美化景观，外出游泳池。“他向一个用吊索抱着婴儿的亲戚挥了挥手。“你能保证我们为子孙后代提供水吗？ ”他问比尔的代表。“你能为她那一代、我的孩子那一代、我的孙子那一代和这个小婴儿那一代保证水吗？ ”

在这场有争议的听证会两天后，图森市议会的一致投票结束了对这片土地的吞并。在随后的会议上，该市通过了针对数据中心和其他大型水用户的新规则。居民们松了一口气，但不会太久。在该市停止吞并三周后，有效地扼杀了开发，当地记者证实，无论如何， Beale正在推进数据中心。县官员和比尔代表此前曾表示，这笔交易取决于图森吞并这片土地。突然间，这不再是一个问题。（ Beale拒绝评论为什么吞并不再是交易的必要条件。）

随着时间的推移，该计划还有其他调整：数据中心将不再采用水冷，而是依靠闭环空气冷却。如果这种转变是为了赢得比尔的批评者，那就行不通了。无沙漠数据中心联盟的成员声称，风冷设施使用更多的电力，而且由于发电厂也使用水来冷却其系统，因此风冷数据中心实际上可能更耗水，只是间接地，这是Beale否认的指控。Beale发言人Tony Burkart告诉The Verge ： “该项目使用风冷技术不会增加整体能源使用量；虽然能源分配不同，但能源使用量是一样的。”（发电确实需要水，尽管关于亚利桑那州发电厂消耗多少水的数据很少。）这一变化也使Beale成为了一名租户：据报道，亚马逊退出了该项目，称风冷设施无法满足其需求。Beale拒绝透露它是否已经为Project Blue找到了新租户。Burkart说： “这取决于我们的租户何时选择宣布他们对项目的投资。”

尽管如此，这个项目还是向前推进了。该县在圣诞节前夕完成了与Beale的交易， Beale承诺以1500万美元的捐款形式带来更多的礼物，其中一些将用于当地的STEM和贸易学校课程。新的一年带来了更多的挑战。该州总检察长就亚利桑那州公用事业监管机构亚利桑那州公司委员会批准Beale和TEP之间的特殊能源协议提起上诉。无沙漠数据中心联盟的成员提起了一项单独的诉讼，指控该县与Beale的交易违反了该州的公开会议法。

Apps in the consumer voice AI world seem to be converging, as Granola, known for its meeting notetaker, launched a dictation feature today. This comes months after Wispr, known for its dictation tool, launched a meeting notetaker.

Granola’s dictation currently works on Mac just like any other such tool. Users can press the “Fn” key and start speaking, and the tool cleans up and formats their speech and posts the final text. This feature works across all apps, so users can post notes, dictate prompts, and reply to emails and messages.
Granola now does voice typing. Unlimited words, for free.Granola already writes your meeting notes. Now it can do the typing for you, in any app. pic.twitter.com/et60VtwWA0
The company said that the feature will land on iOS and Windows soon.

Granola and Wispr are valued at $1.5 billion and $2 billion, respectively. Granola is focused on meeting-related automation and notetaking. On the other hand, Wispr is trying to build its own models through a research lab, which is exploring different human-computer interfaces.

The feature mashups are not exclusive to Granola and Wispr. Other voice startups such as Fireflies, Speechify, and Monologue have converged into multifeature apps with meeting notetaking and dictation capabilities. Until earlier in the year, the play was around having a focused app that does one thing well. But now, all of these apps are thinking about how to get more out of capturing users’ speech.

cards.title: An updated Model Spec for more capable and beneficial AI
cards.title_cn: 更新的模型规格，以实现更强大、更有益的人工智能
cards.summary: 【OpenAI】OpenAI’s updated Model Spec outlines five core values to guide more capable AI toward sound judgment, human agency, and faithfulness to human intent.
fulltext: October 29, 2026

As our models get smarter and take more consequential actions in the world, it becomes increasingly important that they go beyond just interpreting the specific instructions they receive. Models also need to understand human intentions and values, so they can exercise good judgment in situations their instructions don’t explicitly address while remaining faithful to human intent and oversight.

Today we’re updating the Model Spec⁠(opens in a new window), our public description of how we want our models to behave. The update reorganizes its guidance around five underlying values: faithfulness to human intent, harm minimization, honesty and transparency, human agency, and care. This reflects an aim of our work on value alignment: for models to understand and apply human values in unfamiliar situations, while remaining faithful to human intent. Alongside clearer explanations of existing principles, the revision adds guidance on context, oversight, and agency, adjusts some behavioral defaults, and retires much of the detailed style guidance.

The five values above articulate broad commitments already reflected across the Model Spec: serving human purposes, being truthful, minimizing harm, respecting people’s freedom to form their own views, and taking their circumstances seriously. Bringing these commitments together helps explain why the Spec asks models to behave as it does, and helps us develop clearer guidance where those commitments were less fully expressed. This update is another step in our work to refine the Spec through research, experience deploying models, public feedback on the Spec and model behavior, and discussions with users and outside experts.
We want AI to benefit a world of people with different needs, values, and hopes for the future.

Faithfulness to human intent is the foundation of this approach: understanding and helping people pursue what matters to them. OpenAI writes the Spec, sets boundaries, and trains models to respect them; developers direct applications within those boundaries; and users direct the model’s work subject to those constraints. Our models should expand people’s ability to shape their own lives by helping them understand the world, discover possibilities, and pursue the goals they choose, while taking seriously how that assistance affects others. Faithfulness to human intent and the remaining four values organize the Spec and guide how our models should navigate some of the most important trade-offs they face. They are not intended to capture the full range of human values our models should respect and help people pursue.

Faithfulness means going beyond following instructions literally to deeply understanding what OpenAI, developers, and users intend and value, and acting wisely when that understanding is incomplete. It also means recognizing that people’s beliefs and values can change, and helping them reflect and grow in ways they would endorse without quietly steering them or overriding their choices. For example, when helping someone compare job offers, the model might draw on priorities they have shared before—such as predictable hours—while making those assumptions visible and easy to correct.

Our mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. This requires considering not only someone’s immediate intentions, but also their longer-term interests and the effects on others. The other four values make these considerations explicit:
Minimizing harm means respecting firm safety boundaries and accounting for the foreseeable consequences of the model’s actions.
Honesty and transparency mean being truthful about what the model knows, does, and is uncertain about so people can understand and evaluate its reasoning and work.
Facilitating human agency means strengthening people’s ability to understand, choose, and act for themselves.
Care means attending to the circumstances of those affected, following relevant social and professional norms, and doing work people can rely on.

The Spec turns these values into practical guidance, with firm boundaries where needed to protect people and society, and otherwise mostly takes the form of defaults that users and developers can override.

Alongside this Model Spec update, we’ve been exploring new training methods to help our models learn these core values and better understand and follow the Spec’s specific behavioral principles. The aim is to build an understanding of why those principles matter and how to apply them in new situations: to do the right things for the right reasons. We want that understanding to support sound judgment in consequential decisions and care in everyday decisions that can add up to lasting benefits for people and society⁠(opens in a new window). We’ll share results and lessons from this training work in future updates.
This reorganization also helped us identify where additional guidance was needed, develop new principles to address it, and revise or retire existing guidance as needed.

The new section on faithfulness to human intent starts from the idea that what people value is primary, and instructions are ordinarily the clearest and most important signals of those values. This approach borrows from the assistance-games framing of alignment (see early work⁠(opens in a new window) and a later overview⁠(opens in a new window)). The section incorporates an updated chain of command⁠(opens in a new window), which explains which instructions apply and how conflicts are resolved. A new subsection, consider context carefully⁠(opens in a new window), explains how conversations, memories, and other contextual evidence should inform the model’s understanding of people’s intentions and preferences.

We’ve also added defaults on supporting human agency⁠(opens in a new window) and following relevant social norms⁠(opens in a new window), and expanded existing guidance on controlling and communicating side effects⁠(opens in a new window). These principles capture additional, often subtle but important ways the remaining values should surface in model behavior: considering the effects of the work on others, strengthening users’ capabilities, and producing work people can rely on, while respecting the user’s goals and instructions.

At the same time, we’re retiring most of the Spec’s detailed style guidance. Style should adapt to what people prefer—in aggregate, within languages and cultures, and for each person—with user feedback and context providing evidence about those preferences. The Spec retains stronger defaults, such as approaching questions objectively⁠(opens in a new window). Users and developers can explicitly ask the model to take a particular perspective, but the model should not infer that preference merely from what it thinks they want to hear.
Finally, reflecting the increasing breadth of our models’ use cases and deployment settings, we now refer to the model as “GPT” rather than “the assistant” in the Spec.

This update is a first step in making the values and reasoning behind the Spec more explicit as models become more capable. The Model Spec describes the behavior we are working toward; our models do not yet fully reflect it. We will keep improving both the Spec and the models as we learn from research, real-world use, and feedback.

We want to hear which parts of the Spec you find compelling, where you disagree with the balance it strikes, and what it overlooks or leaves unclear. Feedback on the values, trade-offs, and specific language can help us improve it. We invite you to read the updated Model Spec⁠(opens in a new window) and share your perspective⁠(opens in a new window).

cards.summary_cn: 【OpenAI】OpenAI更新的模型规范概述了五个核心价值观，以引导更有能力的人工智能走向合理的判断、人为代理和对人类意图的忠诚。
fulltext_cn: 随着我们的模型变得越来越聪明，并在世界上采取越来越重要的行动，它们不仅仅是解释他们收到的具体指令，这一点变得越来越重要。模型还需要了解人类的意图和价值观，这样他们才能在他们的指示没有明确涉及的情况下做出良好的判断，同时保持对人类意图和监督的忠诚。

今天，我们将更新模型规格（在新窗口中打开） ，这是我们对模型行为的公开描述。此次更新围绕五个基本价值观对其指导进行了重组：忠于人类意图、伤害最小化、诚实和透明、人性化以及关怀。这反映了我们价值观一致性工作的目标：让模型在不熟悉的情况下理解和应用人类价值观，同时忠实于人类意图。除了对现有原则进行更清晰的解释外，该修订还增加了关于背景、监督和代理的指导，调整了一些行为默认值，并淘汰了大部分详细的风格指导。
上述五个价值观阐明了已经反映在模型规范中的广泛承诺：为人类目的服务，诚实，最大限度地减少伤害，尊重人们形成自己观点的自由，并认真对待自己的情况。将这些承诺整合在一起有助于解释为什么规范要求模型像它一样行事，并帮助我们在这些承诺未得到充分表达的情况下制定更明确的指导。此次更新是我们通过研究、部署模型的经验、对规范和模型行为的公众反馈以及与用户和外部专家的讨论来完善规范的又一步骤。
我们希望人工智能造福一个拥有不同需求、价值观和对未来抱有希望的世界。

忠于人类意图是这种方法的基础：理解并帮助人们追求对他们来说重要的事情。OpenAI编写规范，设置边界，并训练模型以尊重它们；开发人员在这些边界内指导应用程序；用户在这些限制下指导模型的工作。我们的模式应该通过帮助人们了解世界、发现可能性和追求他们选择的目标来扩大人们塑造自己生活的能力，同时认真对待这种援助如何影响他人。忠实于人类意图和其余四个价值观组织了规范，并指导我们的模型如何应对他们面临的一些最重要的权衡。它们并非旨在捕捉我们的模型应尊重和帮助人们追求的全部人类价值观。
忠诚意味着超越从字面上遵循指示，深入了解OpenAI、开发人员和用户的意图和价值，并在理解不完整时明智行事。这也意味着认识到人们的信仰和价值观可以改变，并帮助他们以他们认可的方式进行反思和成长，而不会悄悄地引导他们或推翻他们的选择。例如，在帮助某人比较工作机会时，该模型可能会利用他们以前分享过的优先事项（例如可预测的工时） ，同时使这些假设可见且易于纠正。
我们的使命是确保通用人工智能造福全人类。这不仅需要考虑某人的直接意图，还需要考虑他们的长期利益和对他人的影响。其他四个值明确说明了这些考虑因素：
最大限度地减少伤害意味着尊重公司的安全边界，并考虑模型行为的可预见后果。
诚实和透明意味着对模型所知道、所做和不确定的事情保持真实，以便人们能够理解和评估其推理和工作。
促进人的能动性意味着增强人们理解、选择和为自己采取行动的能力。
关怀意味着关注受影响者的情况，遵循相关的社会和职业规范，并做人们可以依靠的工作。
规范将这些价值观转化为实际指导，在需要保护人员和社会的地方有明确的界限，否则大多采取用户和开发人员可以覆盖的默认形式。
除了本次模型规范更新之外，我们一直在探索新的培训方法，以帮助我们的模型学习这些核心价值观，并更好地理解和遵循规范的具体行为原则。目的是了解这些原则的重要性以及如何在新情况下应用它们：出于正确的原因做正确的事情。我们希望这种理解能够支持在重大决策中做出正确的判断，并在日常决策中谨慎行事，从而为人类和社会带来持久的好处（在新窗口中打开）。我们将在未来的更新中分享本次培训工作的成果和教训。
这次重组还有助于我们确定需要额外指导的地方，制定解决问题的新原则，并根据需要修改或淘汰现有指导。

关于忠于人类意图的新章节始于人们最看重的东西，而指示通常是这些价值观最清晰、最重要的信号。这种方法借鉴了对齐的辅助游戏框架（请参阅早期工作⁠（在新窗口中打开）和稍后的概述⁠（在新窗口中打开） ）。该部分包含一个更新的指挥链（在新窗口中打开） ，其中解释了哪些指令适用以及如何解决冲突。一个新的小节，仔细考虑上下文（在新窗口中打开） ，解释了对话、记忆和其他上下文证据应该如何告知模型对人们意图和偏好的理解。
我们还添加了支持人为代理（在新窗口中打开）和遵循相关社会规范（在新窗口中打开）的默认值，并扩展了控制和沟通副作用的现有指南（在新窗口中打开）。这些原则捕捉了模型行为中剩余价值的额外、通常微妙但重要的方式：考虑工作对他人的影响，加强用户的能力，并产生人们可以依赖的工作，同时尊重用户的目标和指示。
与此同时，我们将淘汰规格的大部分详细风格指南。风格应该适应人们的喜好--总的来说，在语言和文化中，针对每个人--用户的反馈和背景为这些偏好提供了证据。规范保留了更强的默认值，例如客观地处理问题（在新窗口中打开）。用户和开发人员可以明确要求模型采取特定的视角，但模型不应该仅仅从它认为他们想要听到的内容来推断这种偏好。
最后，考虑到我们模型的用例和部署设置越来越广泛，我们现在在规范中将模型称为“GPT”而不是“助手”。
随着模型变得更加强大，此更新是使规范背后的价值观和推理更加明确的第一步。模型规格描述了我们正在努力实现的行为；我们的模型尚未完全反映它。随着我们从研究、实际使用和反馈中学习，我们将不断改进规格和模型。
我们想听听您认为规格的哪些部分令人信服，您在哪些方面不同意它所达到的平衡，以及它忽略或不清楚的地方。关于价值观、权衡和特定语言的反馈可以帮助我们改进。我们邀请您阅读更新后的型号规格⁠（在新窗口中打开）并分享您的观点⁠（在新窗口中打开）。

cards.title: Microsoft’s AI future has fewer jobs
cards.title_cn: 微软的人工智能未来工作岗位减少
cards.summary: 【Microsoft】To anyone listening closely to what Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has been saying over the past couple of years, this week felt like the clearest sign yet that AI is about to fundamentally change the si…
fulltext: It’s also time to name the next Elder Scrolls game, and Xbox’s architect of Forza Motorsport is leaving.

To anyone listening closely to what Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella has been saying over the past couple of years, this week felt like the clearest sign yet that AI is about to fundamentally change the size of Microsoft’s workforce. Microsoft is now offering voluntary buyouts to around 60,000 employees across the US, UK, Canada, and India.

It’s the first time the company has presented such an offer to so many employees, expanding greatly upon the retirement offer that was limited to around 9,000 employees earlier this year. It’s all part of an ongoing effort to avoid reducing investment in AI infrastructure by lowering Microsoft’s operating costs and headcount.

“Our total people costs will go down, our cost per head will go up, and my GPU per researcher will go up,” Nadella said on a podcast almost two years ago, responding to a question about AI’s impact on headcount. That’s a financial way of saying Microsoft will have fewer people, but it will offer higher salaries and more tools and AI power to those who remain.

It also helps explain the continued layoffs we’ve seen at Microsoft over the past couple of years. Microsoft has been performing layoffs regularly over the past decade, but over the past couple of years, the layoffs and executive departures have been significant.

These aren’t the annual layoffs of old; they’re now happening every few months. This week’s voluntary exit offer arrived just months after Microsoft laid off 4,800 employees, cuts that impacted its Xbox and commercial sales teams the most.

For the first time in a decade, Microsoft’s overall headcount has also gone down year over year. Microsoft now employs around 223,000 people as of June 30th, 5,000 fewer than the 228,000 people it employed in 2025. Microsoft laid off 4 percent of its workforce in July last year, and it’s now offering voluntary buyout offers to around a quarter of its employees.

More than 30 percent of the 9,000 eligible employees accepted a retirement offer earlier this year, but that number will likely be far less for the company’s latest Voluntary Exit Offer. That’s largely because, according to sources familiar, the offer is practically the same as regular severance terms at Microsoft — cash based on time at the company, accelerated stock vesting, some additional subsidized health coverage, and several months of career services.

But what makes this unusual is the scale of the amount of employees who have been offered this exit. Even if only 5 percent accept the offer, that’s still 3,000 employees. I understand eligible employees have until December to decide, so we won’t know the impact of this offer for a while yet. With rumors of more layoffs in November and January, the amount of employees who do accept will surely inform Microsoft’s numbers for its next round of cuts.

There are some, both inside and outside the company, who think Microsoft needs these cuts. “Microsoft needs fewer people,” says Merill Fernando, a former Microsoft Entra product manager. “I’ve been on the inside. I’ve seen how things get built. Lots of small orgs. Layers on layers. Silos everywhere.”

Fernando paints a picture of a Microsoft where every organization “had its own priorities and its own decision makers,” so it’s hard to get the company to do anything collectively. It sounds a little like the meme where each organization in Microsoft is pointing guns at each other, competing instead of collaborating.

Nadella even addressed that meme last year in a podcast with Stripe co-founder John Collison, acknowledging that the comic has defined Microsoft’s cultural narrative “more so than reality,” but that it had signaled some very real tensions inside the company. “In some sense, some of these divisional tensions are real issues that need to have tension. Social cohesion is not a goal, winning in the marketplace is a goal,” said Nadella.

The question now is whether Nadella can reshape Microsoft for the AI era without undoing the cultural transformation that helped define his leadership. A company that has shifted to be built around empathy is now asking its employees to reckon with an AI future that could make many of their jobs unnecessary. How Nadella handles that transition will define his legacy as much as the growth and success he’s achieved over the past decade.

A few weeks ago I started hearing from Xbox employees that Dan Greenawalt, the longtime creative force behind Forza Motorsport, is leaving after almost 27 years. Greenawalt is departing as the head of Turn 10 Studios, the Forza Motorsport creator that merged with Forza Horizon developer Playground Games.

Playground Games studio head Trevor Williams revealed the news in a recent internal memo, seen by Notepad. “Dan Greenawalt has decided that this is the right time for him to retire from Microsoft,” says Williams. Greenawalt will stay on as an adviser to Williams and the newly appointed Playground Games chief operating officer, Michel Bastien, “while he transitions to his next phase.” Here’s part of Williams’ memo about Greenawalt:

It’s hard to overstate Dan’s impact over the past 27 years. From shipping Project Gotham Racing on the original XBOX in 2001 to leading the creation of Forza, founding Turn 10 Studios and appearing so many times on our E3 stage, usually making a dramatic entrance with a supercar in tow – and so much more – we owe tremendous thanks and gratitude to Dan. On behalf of both teams, I would like to thank Dan for his leadership, his support, and his partnership. I wish him well for whatever comes next.

Microsoft revealed last month that it was merging its two Forza developers into a single studio as part of a massive restructuring of Xbox. Both Playground Games and Turn 10 Studios have merged into just Playground Games. The studio now has two locations: Playground Games Leamington Spa and Playground Games Redmond.

With Greenawalt retiring and Turn 10 merged into Playground Games, it’s not clear if we’ll ever see Microsoft return to Forza Motorsport. More than 70 people at Turn 10 Studios were laid off last year, in a move that hit the vast majority of the studio. Over the past year, Turn 10 Studios has essentially been maintaining Forza Motorsport, and now the remaining employees have moved to Playground Games to work on Forza Horizon and Fable.

It’s been more than eight years since Bethesda officially announced the existence of the sixth game in its Elder Scrolls series. While there have been some debates around platform exclusivity for The Elder Scrolls VI, we’ve heard very little detail about the game that Bethesda has been working on all this time.

Sources familiar with Bethesda’s plans tell me that the Xbox-owned publisher is about to announce that the next Elder Scrolls game will officially be called The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel. The announcement could come as soon as next month, during a period that will mark 15 years since The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim was released.

Bethesda has been showing off Sentinel gameplay in recent months, I’m told. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma got a live playthrough of Sentinel in August, and she praised the scale of the game and said “the story is even greater.”

While I’m only expecting a name reveal next month and nothing more, I’ve been hearing some additional details about the game. If you want to totally avoid spoilers about the game, then don’t read the next paragraph.

I understand that Sentinel will be set in Hammerfell, a province in the Elder Scrolls universe that’s appeared in The Elder Scrolls Adventures: Redguard and The Elder Scrolls Online. Sentinel will be the first game about the history of the Elder Scrolls, and help uncover the secrets of these mysterious ancient artifacts.

cards.summary_cn: 【Microsoft】对于任何密切关注微软首席执行官萨蒂亚·纳德拉（ Satya Nadella ）过去几年所说的话的人来说，本周似乎是人工智能将从根本上改变世界的最明显迹象。
fulltext_cn: 现在也是命名下一个Elder Scrolls游戏的时候了， Xbox的Forza Motorsport架构师即将离开。
对于任何密切关注微软首席执行官萨蒂亚·纳德拉（ Satya Nadella ）过去几年所说的话的人来说，本周似乎是人工智能即将从根本上改变微软员工规模的最明显迹象。微软现在向美国、英国、加拿大和印度的约6万名员工提供自愿收购。
这是该公司首次向如此多的员工提出这样的要约，大大扩展了今年早些时候仅限于约9,000名员工的退休要约。这一切都是通过降低微软的运营成本和员工人数来避免减少人工智能基础设施投资的持续努力的一部分。
“我们的总人力成本将下降，人均成本将上升，每位研究人员的GPU将上升，”纳德拉在近两年前的一个播客中回答了有关人工智能对人数影响的问题。这是一种财务上的说法，微软的人数将减少，但它将为那些留下来的人提供更高的薪水、更多的工具和人工智能能力。
这也有助于解释我们在过去几年中在微软看到的持续裁员。微软在过去十年中一直定期进行裁员，但在过去几年中，裁员和高管离职一直很重要。
这不是以前的年度裁员；现在每隔几个月就会发生一次。本周的自愿退出提议是在微软裁员4,800人几个月后提出的，裁员对其Xbox和商业销售团队的影响最大。
十年来，微软的总体员工人数首次同比下降。截至6月30日，微软目前的员工人数约为223,000人，比2025年的228,000人少5,000人。去年7月，微软裁减了4%的员工，现在它正在向大约四分之一的员工提供自愿收购要约。
今年早些时候，在9000名符合条件的员工中，超过30%的人接受了退休要约，但对于该公司最新的自愿退出要约来说，这个数字可能会少得多。这在很大程度上是因为，据熟悉的消息人士称，该报价实际上与微软的定期离职条款相同--基于公司时间的现金、加速股票归属、一些额外的补贴医疗保险和几个月的职业服务。
但是，让这种情况变得不寻常的是，获得这种退出的员工数量的规模。即使只有5%的人接受报价，这仍然是3,000名员工。我理解符合条件的员工必须在12月之前做出决定，因此我们暂时无法了解此优惠的影响。随着11月和1月更多裁员的传闻，接受裁员的员工人数肯定会告知微软下一轮裁员的数字。
公司内外都有一些人认为微软需要这些削减。“微软需要更少的人，”前微软Entra产品经理Merill Fernando说。“我一直在里面。我已经看到了东西是如何建造的。有很多小型组织。层层叠叠，到处都是筒仓。”
费尔南多描绘了一幅微软的画面，每个组织“都有自己的优先事项和自己的决策者” ，因此很难让公司集体做任何事情。这听起来有点像微软的每个组织都互相指责，竞争而不是合作的模因。
去年，纳德拉甚至在与Stripe联合创始人约翰·科里森（ John Collison ）的播客中谈到了这一模因，承认这部漫画对微软文化叙事的定义“比现实更真实” ，但它表明公司内部存在一些非常真实的紧张关系。“从某种意义上说，其中一些部门紧张关系是需要紧张关系的真正问题。社会凝聚力不是一个目标，在市场上取胜是一个目标，”纳德拉说。
现在的问题是，纳德拉是否能够在人工智能时代重塑微软，而不会破坏有助于定义其领导力的文化转型。一家已经转向以同理心为基础的公司现在要求其员工考虑人工智能的未来，这可能会使他们的许多工作变得不必要。纳德拉如何处理这一转变将定义他的遗产，以及他在过去十年中取得的成长和成功。
几周前，我开始从Xbox员工那里听说， Forza Motorsport背后的长期创意力量Dan Greenawalt在将近27年后即将离职。Greenawalt将担任Turn 10 Studios的负责人，该工作室是与Forza Horizon开发商Playground Games合并的Forza Motorsport创始人。

Playground Games工作室负责人特雷弗·威廉姆斯（ Trevor Williams ）在最近的内部备忘录中透露了这一消息，记事本看到了这一消息。Williams说： “Dan Greenawalt已经决定，现在是他从微软退休的合适时机。” Greenawalt将继续担任Williams和新任命的Playground Games首席运营官Michel Bastien的顾问， “同时他将过渡到下一阶段。以下是Williams关于Greenawalt的备忘录的一部分：
很难夸大Dan在过去27年中的影响。从2001年在原版XBOX上推出Project Gotham Racing到领导Forza的创建，创立Turn 10 Studios ，并在我们的E3舞台上多次亮相，通常以超级跑车作为戏剧性的入口–以及更多–我们非常感谢Dan。我谨代表两个团队感谢Dan的领导、支持和伙伴关系。我祝愿他接下来一切顺利。
微软上个月透露，作为Xbox大规模重组的一部分，它正在将其两个Forza开发人员合并为一个工作室。Playground Games和Turn 10 Studios都已合并为Playground Games。该工作室现在有两个地点： Playground Games Leamington Spa和Playground Games Redmond。

随着Greenawalt退役， Turn 10并入Playground Games ，目前尚不清楚我们是否会看到微软重返Forza Motorsport。去年， Turn 10 Studios的70多人被解雇，此举影响了绝大多数工作室。在过去的一年里， Turn 10 Studios基本上一直在维护Forza Motorsport ，现在剩下的员工已经搬到了Playground Games ，从事Forza Horizon和Fable的工作。
自从贝塞斯达正式宣布《上古卷轴》系列第六款游戏的存在以来，已经过去了八年多。虽然围绕《上古卷轴VI》的平台专属性存在一些争论，但我们很少听到有关Bethesda一直致力于开发的游戏的细节。
熟悉贝塞斯达计划的消息人士告诉我，这家Xbox旗下的发行商即将宣布，下一款《上古卷轴》游戏将正式命名为《上古卷轴VI ：哨兵》。该公告最快可能会在下个月发布，届时将标志着《上古卷轴V ：天际》发行15周年。
据我所知，贝塞斯达最近几个月一直在炫耀《哨兵》的游戏玩法。Xbox首席执行官阿莎·夏尔马（ Asha Sharma ）在8月份获得了Sentinel的现场直播，她称赞了游戏的规模，并说“故事更大。”
虽然我只期待下个月会有一个名字，没有别的了，但我已经听到了一些关于游戏的更多细节。如果您想完全避免破坏游戏，请不要阅读下一段。
据我所知，《哨兵》将设定在《上古卷轴历险记：红卫兵》和《上古卷轴在线》中出现的上古卷轴宇宙的一个省份Hammerfell。《哨兵》将是关于上古卷轴历史的第一款游戏，并有助于揭开这些神秘古代文物的秘密。

cards.title: The NYT Cooking app is testing AI recipe modifications
cards.title_cn: 纽约时报烹饪应用程序正在测试AI食谱修改
cards.summary: 【The Verge】The New York Times is testing a new AI feature for its Cooking app that helps users to modify recipes, and it has sparked some drama among users. Last Friday, NYT Cooking senior editor Genevieve Ko an…
fulltext: Some users aren’t exactly thrilled with The New York Times’ recipe-tweaking AI tool.

The New York Times is testing a new AI feature for its Cooking app that helps users to modify recipes, and it has sparked some drama among users. Last Friday, NYT Cooking senior editor Genevieve Ko announced the feature, which can be used to recommend substitutions for ingredients and cooking equipment, scale recipes to any number of servings, and “generally make our recipes work for what a cook needs at that moment.”

One of the examples given in the article shows a user asking to use baby spinach instead of kale, with the Cooking app feature advising that because baby spinach wilts faster, it should be added during a later step of the recipe. Ko says it can also change the recipes around different pans and tools. Customized recipes are private and can’t be published or shared through the app. The AI modification feature is being rolled out gradually while the NYT monitors how it performs — it’s currently available to all Cooking subscribers on the iOS app, and it will be more broadly available “soon.”

Some NYT readers have pushed back against the feature, citing concerns in the article’s comment section around the environmental impact of widespread AI adoption and the general impact that AI features may have on the user experience. When one user asked if there will be a way to disable the AI feature, Ko responded with, “No, not at this time,” and noted that the feature is “completely optional to use.”

“Unbelievably disappointing to see,” said another NYT user. “I’ve always loved NYT Cooking and it pains me that the AI mandate has reached what used to be a wonderful and simple collection of recipes and notes from all sorts of different people.”

This isn’t the first time that AI has been used by the NYT Cooking app. Ko says it was used to convert imperial volume measurements to metric weight measurements in recipes two years ago, and a feature was added last year that converts recipes to halve or double the original serving size. The comments on the new AI feature announcement post have since been closed, but NYT spokesperson Jordan Cohen tells The Verge that this is standard practice:

“Comments on this article remained open for four days, with editors from Cooking taking care to answer questions, address concerns and engage directly with readers. We kept that conversation open to give readers a meaningful opportunity to share feedback and hear from the team. Closing comments on older articles is standard practice at The Times so that our moderators can focus on new discussions. We’re pleased to see that many members of our Cooking community are interested in exploring this tool and are already trying it out on our iOS app; they’re reporting good results.”

fulltext_cn: 有些用户对《纽约时报》调整食谱的人工智能工具并不十分兴奋。
《纽约时报》正在为其烹饪应用程序测试一项新的人工智能功能，该功能可帮助用户修改食谱，并在用户中引发了一些戏剧性事件。上周五，《纽约时报》烹饪资深编辑Genevieve Ko宣布了这一功能，该功能可用于推荐食材和烹饪设备的替代品，将食谱扩展到任意份量，并“通常使我们的食谱能够满足厨师当时的需求。”
文章中给出的一个示例显示，用户要求使用小菠菜而不是羽衣甘蓝，烹饪应用程序功能建议，由于小菠菜枯萎速度更快，因此应在食谱的后续步骤中添加。Ko说，它还可以改变不同平底锅和工具的食谱。自定义食谱是私密的，无法通过应用发布或共享。人工智能修改功能正在逐步推出，同时纽约时报正在监控其性能--目前iOS应用程序上的所有烹饪订阅者都可以使用它，而且它将“很快”更广泛地使用。
一些《纽约时报》的读者反对这项功能，他们在文章的评论部分提到了广泛采用人工智能对环境的影响以及人工智能功能可能对用户体验产生的一般影响。当一位用户询问是否有办法禁用人工智能功能时， Ko回答说： “不，现在不行” ，并指出该功能是“完全可选的”。
另一位《纽约时报》用户说： “令人难以置信地失望。” “我一直很喜欢纽约时报烹饪， AI的使命已经达到了过去从各种不同的人那里收集的美妙而简单的食谱和笔记，这让我很痛苦。”
这不是纽约时报烹饪应用程序第一次使用人工智能。Ko说，两年前它被用来将英制体积测量转换为配方中的公制重量测量，去年增加了一项功能，将配方转换为原始份量的一半或两倍。此后，对新的人工智能功能公告帖子的评论已被关闭，但纽约时报发言人乔丹·科恩（ Jordan Cohen ）告诉The Verge ，这是标准做法：
“关于这篇文章的评论持续了四天，来自Cooking的编辑会小心翼翼地回答问题、解决问题并直接与读者互动。我们保持对话的开放性，让读者有机会分享反馈并听取团队的意见。结束对旧文章的评论是《泰晤士报》的标准做法，这样我们的主持人就可以专注于新的讨论。我们很高兴看到我们的烹饪社区的许多成员有兴趣探索这个工具，并且已经在我们的iOS应用程序上进行了尝试；他们报告了良好的结果。”

cards.title: Into the Omniverse: How Developers Turn Ideas Into Simulations With Frontier AI Agents
cards.title_cn: 走进全方位：开发人员如何利用前沿人工智能代理将想法转化为模拟
cards.summary: 【NVIDIA】Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. Developers are combining frontier AI mo…
fulltext: Share This Article
Your browser doesn't support HTML5 video. Here is a link to the video instead.

Turning a simulation idea into a working application means assembling assets, connecting physics and rendering, and checking that the scene behaves as intended. Developers are combining frontier AI models with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to help carry out that work — building applications for exploring scenarios, investigating failures and improving designs.
Developers direct AI agents through natural-language instructions, review results and guide changes. Omniverse libraries provide GPU-accelerated physics, rendering and sensor simulation capabilities.
Explore the projects below to see frontier AI models such as GPT-6 Astra at work, and check back for new examples from NVIDIA teams and developers across the ecosystem.

Planning warehouse automation requires a model of the building itself, but shelving and machinery can obscure its structure in site scans. Omniverse brings together real-to-sim tools and agent skills to help developers turn real-world captures into editable starting environments for physical AI simulation.

David Wehr, from NVIDIA’s simulation technology team, built on that work using Astra to develop a workflow for digitally reconstructing a building without its contents. The goal is an editable, simulation-ready building model where developers can add or reposition shelving and machinery to evaluate warehouse layouts and automation plans before making physical changes.

Wehr guided Astra to interpret panoramic photos, create building geometry and align it with point-cloud measurements. OpenUSD stores the models, while Omniverse’s ovrtx library renders results for inspection.
Explore NVIDIA Omniverse agent skills to help agents build with Omniverse libraries.

Before changing how industrial equipment operates, engineers need a way to explore the consequences. Pradeep Kaushik, a member of the NVIDIA Omniverse developer relations team, directed Astra to build a what-if analysis application around a simulated gas turbine and generator.

The application lets users adjust conditions such as load, ambient temperature and fuel composition, then compare power, efficiency, fuel consumption and equipment response. Six test procedures explore scenarios including load changes, a stuck fuel valve and an exhaust-sensor error.
The prototype gives engineers an interactive way to investigate how operating changes and faults could affect equipment behavior, supporting decisions about which scenarios warrant further testing.

Astra used tools like Cantera for thermochemistry and SciPy for equipment dynamics. The application maps solver results to rotor animation and color-coded temperature, pressure and flow-velocity indicators in a 3D turbine. NVIDIA Omniverse libraries update the scene (ovstage), render it with RTX (ovrtx) and stream the view to the browser (ovstream). Engineers can rotate and zoom the cutaway, switch between indicators, and pause or scrub through a simulated response alongside charts and virtual instruments.

With SimReady Central Library, announced at GTC Berlin, developers can access more than 2,000 simulation-ready USD assets from equipment manufacturers and asset providers for robotics simulations and AI factory digital twins workflows.

Paul Kind, a member of NVIDIA’s Omniverse documentation team, pointed an AI agent to the library and guided scene assembly through conversation. His kitchen scene included 180 placements drawn from 63 unique library assets, alongside 18 custom geometry pieces. Kind reviewed renders produced with Isaac Sim and guided further adjustments.
For robotics and factory workflows, developers can select SimReady assets with the simulation properties embedded to fit their required task then test in an assembled environment.
Find assets in SimReady Central Library, and learn how to contribute.
A warehouse simulation needs to keep running smoothly as more robot arms, conveyors and boxes fill the scene.

When it slows down, developers need to identify what’s holding it back. Bhavik Sanganee, principal engineer at NVIDIA, used Astra with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to build a warehouse simulation, increase its complexity and investigate slowdowns.

Performance first fell below the target when the scene doubled in size. Running physics calculations, image rendering and video preparation concurrently restored performance and enabled further scaling.
With 80 conveyors, 40 arms and 800 boxes, the simulation sustained 30 frames per second at full HD resolution during a two-minute test. The arms completed 640 successful box placements.
Doubling the scene again reduced performance. Testing traced the slowdown to the physics and robot-control pipeline, giving Sanganee a specific area to improve.
Start building with NVIDIA Omniverse libraries.

In electronics assembly, a robot may need to position a flexible cable around components before plugging it into a port. The cable bends as the robot moves it, and the connector must line up precisely to fit.

Oyindamola Omotuyi, robotics technical marketing manager at NVIDIA, directed Astra to build a robot simulation using NVIDIA Isaac Lab, Newton physics and Omniverse rendering with a Robotiq gripper handling the cable.

Astra also developed a reinforcement learning system that combined learned cable-routing movements with position-and-orientation feedback and corrective adjustments for USB-C insertion. The simulation gave Omotuyi a way to test cable handling and connector alignment before moving to physical-robot experiments.
The controller used information supplied directly by the simulation. Next steps include testing a friction-held grasp and using information a physical robot could obtain from cameras and sensors.
Get started with robot learning in NVIDIA Isaac Lab.

Before testing whether a robot can pick up and move a box, developers need a simulation model with joints that move correctly and with grippers that can hold the object. A computer-aided design (CAD) model provides the robot’s shape, but it still needs physics properties to perform the task.

Using an ABB Robotics YuMi robot, developers directed Astra with NVIDIA Omniverse content libraries to convert CAD files into OpenUSD, match the robot’s appearance to reference images, and configure joints and collision geometry. They checked the asset against SimReady Foundation requirements before testing it in NVIDIA Isaac Sim.

Both arms and grippers completed four cube pick-and-place cycles, using simulated finger contact and friction. These tests demonstrated behavior under the simulated conditions — estimated physical properties were not calibrated against the real robot.
Explore a gamified, physics-based control of a humanoid robot in first- and third-person view.

Before automating warehouse tasks, developers need an interactive simulation environment to explore task behavior and evaluate how the work gets done. Frank DeLise, Omniverse product manager at NVIDIA, used Astra to turn a SimReady warehouse and humanoid robot into an interactive simulator with first- and third-person views.

DeLise directed Astra to connect NVIDIA Omniverse libraries for physics (ovphysx), scene updates (ovstage), rendering (ovrtx) and the user interface (ovui). He also used Astra with SimReady (simready-foundation) to create the physical scene in simulation. Astra then generated animation and application code to bring those capabilities together.
Learn how to prepare and validate SimReady robot assets with frontier AI models and NVIDIA Omniverse libraries.

Changing a scene, sensor or driving model can significantly affect autonomous-vehicle simulations. Doyub Kim, a manager on the simulation technology team at NVIDIA, asked Astra to build Zero to Alpamayo — a reusable simulation environment based on San Francisco’s Market Street.

Kim directed Astra to map out the workflow, then connect asset creation, traffic, Omniverse RTX sensor simulation and Alpamayo driving in stages, checking each integration. The resulting prototype was a testing ground for comparing models and tracing how scene or sensor changes affect downstream driving behavior. A separate Cosmos3-Nano experiment varied weather and lighting in recorded simulation videos, allowing Kim to compare the driving model’s responses to the same scenario under different conditions.
Comparing recorded and simulated camera and lidar outputs gives developers key performance indicator-based feedback for refining a scene.

To test robots and autonomous vehicles, developers need to know how closely simulated sensors match real ones. Ashley Reid, who works on RTX sensor validation at NVIDIA, directed Astra and Claude Fable 5 agents to compare ovrtx camera and raw LiDAR outputs with recorded data. The agents created two digital twins from scratch and improved two existing ones. Over about three days, Reid guided an iterative workflow in which agents measured differences, created or modified OpenUSD scenes, and checked the results. Changes addressed missing objects, geometry and materials, with acceptance depending on camera and LiDAR metrics. This gives developers a way to use measured discrepancies to guide scene creation and improvement.
Start by rendering an OpenUSD scene with the ovrtx minimal Python example, then define a sensor measure to compare with recorded data.

Teaching robots new movements means checking whether those actions work under physical constraints. Tae Kim, who leads NVIDIA Omniverse engineering and product, used sports videos and natural-language instructions to guide Astra in building Robo Olympics, an experimental project that tests simulated Unitree G1 humanoids performing sports movements.

Under Kim’s direction, Astra built controllers and refined them through physics trials. Newton Physics Engine simulated behavior, the open source NVIDIA Warp framework accelerated calculations and ovrtx rendered scenes and virtual-camera images. In one experiment, the robot cleared a single hurdle in 64 of 100 simulation trials. The trials gave Kim feedback for improving the robot’s timing and control.
Watch Kim explore building simulations with Astra and NVIDIA Omniverse libraries.

Before a robot can disassemble a product, developers need to know whether its tools can reach and remove the parts. Jens Jebens, a senior product manager for OpenUSD at NVIDIA, directed Astra to model a car suspension in PTC Onshape and configure it in NVIDIA Isaac Sim.

With Astra, Jebens explored computer-aided design and tooling revisions for robots informed by simulation. The agent measured the available space and designed a wrench the robot could use to reach the suspension’s bolts. Jebens reported successful removal of a suspension component in simulation. This connects design and tooling decisions to disassembly results, offering a starting point for robot policy training.
Explore the Onshape importer guide.

Turning 3D models into an application requires connecting assets, live data and an interface. Nic Johns, an engineering director at NVIDIA, prompted Astra to assemble NASA assets into an OpenUSD International Space Station model with telemetry. Johns built the application with a single prompt, then used a follow-up prompt to shift the scene to Earth’s daytime side so the planet was visible.

The workflow used Blender for asset preparation and Omniverse libraries for rendering (ovrtx), scene runtime (ovstage) and streaming (ovstream). The application brings 3D models and operational data into the browser, with Johns guiding its development through prompts and corrections.
Try the Omniverse Real-Time Viewer skill.

A digitally reconstructed room needs editable objects and accurate physical behavior before developers can test interactions. Chirag Majithia, from the Isaac engineering applications team at NVIDIA, directed Astra to turn stereo camera captures into an editable OpenUSD studio.

The workflow combined PyCuSFM, FoundationStereo and nvblox for reconstruction, with user review guiding object selection and placement. Astra assembled generated and Blender-authored assets and used USD Content Agents to configure how objects move and interact in simulation. Isaac Sim tests guided collision and contact revisions for doors and drawers. The studio connects captured geometry to interaction testing, making gaps and object behavior easier to inspect.
Explore USD Content Agents.
Have a simulation idea? Explore NVIDIA Omniverse libraries to start building with an AI agent.

cards.summary_cn: 【NVIDIA】将模拟创意转化为工作应用程序意味着组装资源，连接物理和渲染，并检查场景是否按预期运行。开发商正在将前沿人工智能技术相结合……
fulltext_cn: 分享这篇文章
您的浏览器不支持HTML5视频。这里是视频的链接。
将模拟创意转化为工作应用程序意味着组装资源，连接物理和渲染，并检查场景是否按预期运行。开发人员正在将前沿人工智能模型与NVIDIA Omniverse库相结合，以帮助开展这项工作--构建用于探索场景、调查故障和改进设计的应用程序。
开发人员通过自然语言指令指导AI代理，查看结果并指导更改。Omniverse库提供GPU加速物理、渲染和传感器模拟功能。
浏览以下项目，了解GPT-6 Astra等前沿人工智能模型，并查看整个生态系统中NVIDIA团队和开发人员的新示例。
规划仓库自动化需要建筑物本身的模型，但货架和机械可能会在现场扫描中模糊其结构。Omniverse将真实到模拟的工具和代理技能结合在一起，帮助开发人员将真实世界的捕获转化为可编辑的物理AI模拟起始环境。
NVIDIA模拟技术团队的David Wehr使用Astra开发了一个工作流程，用于数字化重建没有内容的建筑物。目标是建立一个可编辑、可模拟的建筑模型，开发人员可以在其中添加或重新定位货架和机械，以便在进行物理更改之前评估仓库布局和自动化计划。
Wehr引导Astra解读全景照片，创建建筑几何形状并将其与点云测量值对齐。OpenUSD存储模型，而Omniverse的ovrtx库渲染结果以供检查。
探索NVIDIA Omniverse代理技能，帮助代理使用Omniverse库进行构建。
在改变工业设备的运行方式之前，工程师需要一种方法来探索其后果。NVIDIA Omniverse开发者关系团队成员Pradeep Kaushik指示Astra围绕模拟燃气轮机和发电机构建假设分析应用程序。
该应用程序允许用户调整负载、环境温度和燃油成分等条件，然后比较功率、效率、燃油消耗和设备响应。六个测试程序探索了负载变化、燃油阀卡住和排气传感器错误等场景。
该原型为工程师提供了一种交互式方式来研究操作变化和故障如何影响设备行为，从而支持关于哪些场景需要进一步测试的决策。

Astra使用Cantera等工具进行热化学分析，并使用SciPy进行设备动态分析。该应用程序将求解器结果映射到3D涡轮机中的转子动画和颜色编码的温度、压力和流速指示器。NVIDIA Omniverse库更新场景（ ovstage ） ，使用RTX （ ovrtx ）渲染场景，并将视图流式传输到浏览器（ ovstream ）。工程师可以旋转和缩放剖面，在指示器之间切换，并在图表和虚拟仪器旁边通过模拟响应暂停或擦洗。
借助在GTC柏林发布的SimReady中央图书馆，开发人员可以访问来自设备制造商和资产提供商的2,000多项模拟就绪的美元资产，用于机器人模拟和人工智能工厂数字孪生工作流程。
NVIDIA Omniverse文档团队成员Paul Kind将AI代理指向库，并引导场景组装进行对话。他的厨房场景包括来自63个独特图书馆资产的180个展示位置，以及18个定制几何作品。使用Isaac Sim制作的实物审核渲染，并指导进一步的调整。
对于机器人和工厂工作流程，开发人员可以选择嵌入模拟属性的SimReady资产，以适应他们所需的任务，然后在组装环境中进行测试。
在SimReady中央图书馆中查找素材，并了解如何做出贡献。
随着更多机器人手臂、输送机和箱子充满场景，仓库模拟需要保持平稳运行。
当它变慢时，开发人员需要确定是什么阻碍了它。NVIDIA首席工程师Bhavik Sanganee使用Astra与NVIDIA Omniverse库构建仓库模拟，增加其复杂性并调查放缓情况。
当场景尺寸翻倍时，性能首次低于目标。运行物理计算、图像渲染和视频准备可同时恢复性能并实现进一步扩展。
模拟使用80个输送机、40个臂和800个盒子，在两分钟的测试中，以全高清分辨率保持每秒30帧。手臂完成了640次成功的盒子放置。
场景再次翻倍降低了性能。测试将减速追溯到物理和机器人控制管道，为Sanganee提供了一个需要改进的特定区域。
开始使用NVIDIA Omniverse库构建。
在电子组件中，机器人可能需要将柔性电缆定位在组件周围，然后再将其插入端口。电缆在机器人移动时弯曲，连接器必须精确对齐。
NVIDIA机器人技术营销经理Oyindamola Omotuyi指示Astra使用NVIDIA Isaac Lab、Newton物理学和Omniverse渲染构建机器人模拟，并使用Robotiq抓手处理电缆。
Astra还开发了一种强化学习系统，该系统将学到的电缆路由运动与位置和方向反馈以及USB-C插入的校正调整相结合。模拟为Omotuyi提供了一种在进行物理机器人实验之前测试电缆处理和连接器对准的方法。
控制器使用模拟直接提供的信息。接下来的步骤包括测试摩擦抓握，并使用物理机器人可以从摄像头和传感器获得的信息。
在NVIDIA Isaac实验室开始机器人学习。
在测试机器人是否可以拾取和移动盒子之前，开发人员需要一个模拟模型，其中关节可以正确移动，夹具可以夹住物体。计算机辅助设计（ CAD ）模型提供了机器人的形状，但它仍然需要物理属性来执行任务。
使用ABB Robotics YuMi机器人，开发人员使用NVIDIA Omniverse内容库指导Astra将CAD文件转换为OpenUSD ，将机器人的外观与参考图像匹配，并配置关节和碰撞几何形状。在NVIDIA Isaac Sim中测试之前，他们根据SimReady Foundation的要求检查了资产。
手臂和抓手都使用模拟的手指接触和摩擦完成了四个立方体拾取和放置循环。这些测试证明了在模拟条件下的行为—估计的物理特性没有针对真实机器人进行校准。
在第一和第三人称视图中探索人形机器人的游戏化、基于物理的控制。
在自动化仓库任务之前，开发人员需要一个交互式模拟环境来探索任务行为并评估工作的完成方式。NVIDIA Omniverse产品经理Frank DeLise使用Astra将SimReady仓库和人形机器人转变为具有第一和第三人称视图的交互式模拟器。
DeLise指示Astra连接NVIDIA Omniverse库，用于物理（ ovphysx ）、场景更新（ ovstage ）、渲染（ ovrtx ）和用户界面（ ovui ）。他还使用Astra与SimReady （ simready-foundation ）在模拟中创建物理场景。然后， Astra生成动画和应用程序代码，将这些功能整合在一起。
了解如何使用前沿AI模型和NVIDIA Omniverse库准备和验证SimReady机器人资产。
改变场景、传感器或驾驶模型会对自动驾驶汽车的模拟产生重大影响。NVIDIA仿真技术团队经理Doyub Kim要求Astra构建Zero to Alpamayo ，这是一个基于旧金山Market Street的可重用仿真环境。
Kim指示Astra绘制工作流程，然后分阶段连接资产创建、流量、Omniverse RTX传感器模拟和Alpamayo驾驶，检查每个集成。由此产生的原型是比较模型和跟踪场景或传感器变化如何影响下游驾驶行为的试验场。单独的Cosmos3-Nano实验在录制的模拟视频中改变了天气和照明，使Kim能够比较驾驶模型在不同条件下对相同场景的响应。
比较记录和模拟的摄像头和激光雷达输出，为开发人员提供基于关键性能指标的反馈，以优化场景。

为了测试机器人和自动驾驶汽车，开发人员需要知道模拟传感器与真实传感器的匹配程度。在NVIDIA从事RTX传感器验证工作的Ashley Reid指示Astra和Claude Fable 5代理将OVRTX摄像头和原始LiDAR输出与记录的数据进行比较。代理从头开始创建了两个数字孪生体，并改进了两个现有的数字孪生体。在大约三天的时间里， Reid指导了一个迭代工作流程，其中客服代表测量差异，创建或修改OpenUSD场景，并检查结果。更改解决了丢失的物体、几何形状和材料，接受程度取决于摄像头和激光雷达指标。这为开发人员提供了一种使用测量的差异来指导场景创建和改进的方法。
首先使用ovrtx最小Python示例渲染OpenUSD场景，然后定义传感器度量值以与记录的数据进行比较。
教机器人新的动作意味着检查这些动作是否在物理约束下工作。负责NVIDIA Omniverse工程和产品的Tae Kim使用体育视频和自然语言指导Astra构建机器人奥运会，这是一个实验项目，用于测试模拟Unitree G1人形机器人进行体育运动。
在Kim的指导下， Astra制造了控制器，并通过物理试验对其进行了改进。牛顿物理引擎模拟行为，开源NVIDIA Warp框架加速了计算和OVRTX渲染场景和虚拟摄像机图像。在一个实验中，机器人在100次模拟试验中的64次中清除了一个障碍。这些试验为Kim提供了改善机器人时序和控制的反馈。
观看Kim探索Astra和NVIDIA Omniverse库的建筑模拟。
在机器人拆卸产品之前，开发人员需要知道其工具是否可以触及和移除零件。NVIDIA OpenUSD高级产品经理Jens Jebens指示Astra在PTC Onshape中模拟汽车悬架，并在NVIDIA Isaac Sim中进行配置。
通过Astra ， Jebens探索了计算机辅助设计和模拟机器人的工具修订。代理测量了可用空间，并设计了机器人可用于到达悬架螺栓的扳手。Jebens报告在模拟中成功移除了悬浮液组分。这将设计和工具决策与拆卸结果联系起来，为机器人策略培训提供了起点。
浏览Onshape导入工具指南。
将3D模型转化为应用程序需要连接资产、实时数据和界面。NVIDIA的工程总监Nic Johns促使Astra将NASA的资产组装成具有遥测功能的OpenUSD国际空间站模型。Johns用一个提示构建了应用程序，然后使用后续提示将场景转移到地球的白天一侧，以便地球可见。
工作流程使用Blender进行资产准备，并使用Omniverse库进行渲染（ ovrtx ）、场景运行时（ ovstage ）和流式传输（ ovstream ）。该应用程序将3D模型和操作数据带入浏览器， Johns通过提示和纠正来指导其开发。
尝试Omniverse实时查看器技能。
工作流程结合了PyCuSFM、FoundationStereo和nvblox进行重建，用户审核指导对象选择和放置。Astra汇集了生成的和Blender创作的资产，并使用USD内容代理来配置对象在模拟中的移动和交互方式。Isaac Sim测试门和抽屉的引导碰撞和接触修正。工作室将捕获的几何形状连接到交互测试，使间隙和物体行为更容易检查。
探索美元内容代理。
有模拟创意吗？探索NVIDIA Omniverse库，开始使用AI代理构建。
